primitives.name: Jamming Detection Graph
primitives.verbatim_quote: We propose JaGNet, a single-layer heterogeneous graph convolutional LSTM over star graphs of the receiver and its satellites, which, from the standard receiver output alone, detects the jamming, identifies its type and power, and corrects the reported position only when jamming is detected.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'G_t': 'star graph of receiver and satellites at time t', 'H': 'heterogeneous graph convolutional LSTM operator', '\\hat{c}_t': 'detected jammer type at time t', '\\hat{Y}_t': 'position correction vector at time t'}
primitives.assumptions: Receiver output includes standard NMEA data; jamming causes satellite edge removal in graph.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When jamming power exceeds 10 dB C/N0 drop threshold.

layer2.mapping: Graph structure maps to satellite connectivity loss under jamming; LSTM learns temporal evolution of graph features for classification.
layer2.telemetry: Detection rate (99.8–99.9%) and false positive rate (≤1.0%).

primitives.name: Position Error Correction
primitives.verbatim_quote: It reduces the mean absolute position error by 67.5% at held-out locations and by 64.0% on held-out route repetitions, where its error is 20.2 cm below that of the strongest baseline, whereas at the static locations the attentionbased baselines are within 0.4 cm of it.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'p_t': 'reported position at time t', '\\hat{p}_t': 'corrected position at time t', '\\Delta_{lat}, \\Delta_{lon}': 'latitude and longitude deviations in meters'}
primitives.assumptions: Correction applied only after confirmed jamming; baseline models do not account for jamming-induced topology change.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Static locations show minimal error due to attention mechanism; dynamic routes benefit more from graph-based correction.

layer2.mapping: Error kernel derived from graph embedding difference between jammed and clean epochs; correction vector computed via learned residual map.
layer2.telemetry: Mean absolute error reduction of 64–67.5% compared to baseline.

primitives.name: Jamming Identification
primitives.verbatim_quote: JaGNet detects 99.8 to 99.9% of the jammed 10-s windows with at most 1.0% false positives, against 64.7 to 66.2% for the receiver's own monitor, and identifies the jammer type in 95.2 to 96.6% of them.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\hat{c}_t': 'estimated jammer class at time t', 'C': 'set of jammer classes (CW, 3×CW, FM)', 'P(\\hat{c}_t | G_t)': 'conditional probability of jammer type given graph'}
primitives.assumptions: Jammer types are distinguishable through spectral and temporal patterns in satellite data.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Failure occurs when jammer power < 10 dB C/N0 drop or signal overlaps with navigation bands.

layer2.mapping: Jamming type classification mirrors graph node feature clustering; each class corresponds to distinct graph embedding clusters.
layer2.telemetry: Type identification accuracy of 95.2–96.6%; false positive rate ≤1.0%.

reasoning_traces.think:
JaGNet operates on a temporal graph of receiver-satellite interactions, where jamming manifests as edge removal in the star graph. The model uses a heterogeneous graph convolutional LSTM to process time-series satellite data (C/N0, azimuth, elevation) and detect anomalies in satellite connectivity. The architecture leverages the fact that jamming disrupts the satellite mesh, causing loss of tracking and thus altering the graph structure. This is modeled as a topological failure rather than a signal degradation. The LSTM component captures temporal dependencies in the graph features, enabling detection of short-duration jamming events. Once detected, the system infers jammer type and power from the pattern of graph disruption and applies a learned correction function to the reported position. The correction is only applied when jamming is confirmed, avoiding unnecessary adjustments during normal operation. This approach differs from prior methods that rely on raw pseudorange residuals or multipath-specific corrections, making it suitable for low-cost receivers with closed firmware.
